finalExcerpt:
I fixed the bug, and all 5 tests pass (`python3 -m unittest tests.test_inventory`).

`parse_price` in `inventory.py` now treats commas as thousands separators when the string is either of these:
- Comma groups of exactly three digits followed by a decimal part, such as `"1,234.50"`.
- Two or more comma groups, such as `"1,234,567"`.

Everything else still goes through the old decimal-comma path, so `"12,50"` still gives 12.5. I didn't touch `total_value`. I added a regression test in `tests/test_inventory.py` covering `"1,234.50"`, `"$1,234,567"` and `"1,234,567.89"`.

A lone `"1,234"` still parses as 1.234 (decimal comma). The issue's rule only counts a comma group as thousands when a dot or another comma group follows, so I kept that. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` fails because `tests/` isn't a package, which was already the case before my change.
